forces.title: Payments Value Shifts to Invisible Control Layer and Agentic Rails
forces.description: The global payments industry is undergoing a structural transition where value is migrating from visible front-end screens to an invisible back-end 'control layer' involving trust, dynamic routing, and autonomous software agents. This shift means that future growth for digital financial services will depend less on traditional transaction processing and more on capabilities in machine identity, consent engines, and dynamic routing protocols. This fundamentally alters competitive dynamics, requiring DFS providers to invest in underlying infrastructure and AI capabilities.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI Threatens Traditional Payments and Deposit Revenue Pools
forces.description: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is projected to put $75 billion to $160 billion of global payments revenue at risk by 2030, primarily impacting deposit net interest income ($65 billion) and consumer credit card revenues ($10 billion). This disruption stems from AI agents automatically sweeping idle cash to higher-yielding accounts and optimizing payment routing to minimize fees or maximize rewards. For digital financial services heavily reliant on traditional deposit yields or card-based revenue, this presents a significant headwind, necessitating a rapid shift in business models and value capture strategies.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Payment Infrastructure Fragmenting into Regional Multi-Rail Competitive Arenas
forces.description: Rather than converging, global payment infrastructure is fragmenting into regional, multi-rail competitive landscapes. Institutions must navigate diverse pressures from zero-fee domestic real-time account-to-account (A2A) networks, legacy card perimeters, and wholesale stablecoin corridors for cross-border settlement. This fragmentation, driven partly by geopolitical and regulatory divergence, poses a challenge for digital financial services seeking global scalability but also creates opportunities for regional specialists. DFS providers need robust strategies for multi-rail interoperability and compliance across varied market structures.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Rising Demand for Embedded Finance and Software-Driven Value-Added Services
forces.description: There is an increasing concentration of gross profit in software and workflow layers surrounding transactions, with embedded payments, value-added services, and software subscriptions accounting for 40-60% of gross profit for software-led acquirers. Value-added services command significantly higher gross margins (up to 80%) compared to base processing (20-30%). This shift transforms payments into an integrated feature of enterprise workflows, providing a strong tailwind for digital financial services, especially embedded finance models, which can capture higher value by integrating directly into business operations.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: India's Digital Public Infrastructure Enabling Widespread Digital Payments
forces.description: India's digital public infrastructure, exemplified by UPI and Aadhaar, has demonstrated population-scale participation in digital payments, with the RBI Digital Payments Index rising over 5x from March 2018 to September 2025. This robust, interoperable, and state-orchestrated real-time account-to-account (A2A) infrastructure continues to absorb cash flows, making instant payments the dominant standard. This widespread digital adoption provides a foundational tailwind for digital financial services, lowering barriers to entry for fintechs and facilitating scalable digital lending and payment-centric business models.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Interoperable Digital Layer for Enhanced B2B Cash-Flow Based Lending
forces.description: The proposed single, centralized interoperable layer for India's B2B commerce aims to digitize the entire order-to-cash cycle, connecting ERPs, banks, and financiers through standardized APIs. This will enable invoice-level IDs, automated matching, and real-time reconciliation, creating a verifiable transaction ledger. This infrastructure is a significant upside driver for digital credit platforms, as buyer-confirmed invoices can convert ~INR 8 lakh crore of delayed MSME receivables into financeable records, shifting underwriting from collateral to reliable cash flow and addressing the substantial MSME credit gap.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Persistent MSME Credit Gap and B2B Transactional Inefficiencies
forces.description: India's MSME sector faces a credit gap exceeding INR 60 lakh crore, with over 70% being short-term working capital demand. Smaller enterprises are significantly underserved by formal channels (30-40% debt fulfillment). This is compounded by B2B transactional inefficiencies, including manual processing, disconnected systems for invoices and payments, and delayed reconciliation. These factors increase working capital pressure for MSMEs and make cash-flow based lending difficult due to a lack of unified, formal, digital information, presenting a critical challenge that digital lending platforms aim to solve.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Integration of Advanced Analytics and Generative AI for Credit Underwriting
forces.description: The integration of advanced analytics and generative AI is poised to significantly enhance digital financial services, particularly in credit. These technologies can provide cash-flow intelligence, dynamic risk scoring, and agentic credit underwriting, ultimately orchestrating the entire trade lifecycle from end to end for B2B transactions. This capability offers a substantial upside for digital credit platforms, allowing for more precise, automated, and efficient lending decisions, especially for MSMEs, by leveraging deeper insights from verifiable transaction data.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Global Fintech Investment Gaining Momentum with Capital Concentration
forces.description: Global fintech investment saw a significant uptick, rising from $72.2 billion in H2 2025 to $103.1 billion in H1 2026. This momentum signals growing investor confidence in the sector, particularly for scalable platforms in digital assets and AI. However, deal volume remains soft, indicating that capital is concentrated on large deals involving mature fintechs with proven business models and market leadership. This trend suggests a favorable funding environment for established digital financial services companies but potentially a more challenging landscape for early-stage ventures seeking capital.

forces.title: Geopolitical and Macroeconomic Uncertainties Dampening APAC Fintech Investment
forces.description: The APAC region experienced a decline in fintech investment during H1 2026, falling from $7.1 billion to $4.6 billion. This softness is attributed to a combination of ongoing geopolitical tensions, the outbreak of war in the Middle East, and concerns related to inflation and interest rates, which kept investors cautious. This macro-environmental headwind means digital financial services and lending companies in the APAC region may face a more challenging fundraising environment, potentially slowing growth and market expansion compared to regions with more stable conditions.

forces.title: Increased Regulatory Compliance Burden from RBI's New Tech Master Directions
forces.description: The RBI issued consolidated Master Directions on Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework and Digital Payment Security Controls Directions on July 31, 2026. These directives establish comprehensive security and governance frameworks across regulated entities, including credit-card-issuing NBFCs and Payments Banks. While enhancing trust, these new regulations impose a significant compliance burden on digital financial services providers, requiring substantial investment in technology governance, cybersecurity, and fraud prevention controls. This could raise operational costs and pose a challenge for smaller, less resourced fintechs.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: Cross-Border Payments Transforming into Embedded Features, Not Stand-Alone Products
forces.description: The cross-border payments industry is undergoing a structural reset, moving away from being a stand-alone product to becoming an embedded feature within broader financial and operational workflows. This means that for banks and fintech specialists, success will increasingly depend on integrating payments directly into accounting, procurement, and treasury systems. This transformation is a significant opportunity for digital financial services to offer embedded finance solutions that automate entire order-to-cash and procure-to-pay cycles, moving beyond basic money movement to solve complex operational challenges for businesses.
forces.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

forces.title: Commoditization of Core Cross-Border Payment Execution Capabilities
forces.description: Traditional differentiators in cross-border payments—security, speed, and cost—are rapidly becoming table stakes due to fintech competition, technology modernization, and regulatory mandates. This commoditization, exacerbated by increased pricing transparency and growing compliance complexity, leads to margin squeeze. Digital financial services that focus solely on efficient payment execution will face increasing pressure to reduce fees and FX spreads, necessitating a shift towards value-added services and embedded solutions to maintain profitability and differentiation in the market.
forces.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

forces.title: Microfinance Evolution with Tighter Guardrails and Product Diversification
forces.description: The microfinance sector is strengthening due to tighter lending guardrails (MFIN 1.02 and 2.03) that address borrower overleveraging and enhance origination discipline, leading to improved asset quality and healthier new originations. Additionally, NBFC-MFIs are diversifying into individual and non-microfinance lending segments, reducing reliance on Joint Liability Group-based lending. This evolution, supported by relaxed qualifying-asset requirements, provides a positive outlook for financial inclusion tech and digital credit platforms within microfinance, enabling more disciplined growth and expanded product offerings.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Enhanced Technology-Enabled Credit Assessment and Early-Warning Systems in Microfinance
forces.description: The microfinance industry is increasingly adopting technology for credit assessment and monitoring, utilizing borrower-level data to evaluate indebtedness and repayment behavior more effectively. Strengthened credit-bureau reporting standards (daily data mandated by MFIN Guardrails 2.0) and the deployment of analytics and early-warning systems facilitate timely identification and intervention for emerging portfolio stress. This technological advancement significantly benefits financial inclusion tech and digital credit platforms by improving credit decisions, limiting excessive borrower leverage, and strengthening overall portfolio quality and risk management.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

forces.title: Inequitable Funding Access Leading to Microfinance Sector Consolidation
forces.description: Funding conditions for microfinance have improved, but access remains heavily skewed towards larger MFIs, which accounted for approximately 98% of incremental borrowings in FY26. Medium and small institutions continue to face constrained access and higher costs, raising borrowings significantly less relative to their AUM. This inequitable funding access is expected to lead to a contraction in smaller MFIs' balance sheets and sector consolidation, posing a key risk for smaller financial inclusion tech and digital lending platforms struggling to secure capital for growth, despite the overall sector recovery.
forces.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI Poised to Reshape Payments Profit Pools Significantly by 2030
viewpoints.description: McKinsey suggests that agentic artificial intelligence (AI) will materially reshape profit pools in the payments industry well before its full impact is reflected in total industry revenue. The technology could place $75 billion to $160 billion of global payments revenue at risk by 2030, primarily from deposit net interest income and consumer credit card revenues. This creates a significant challenge for traditional models within digital financial services, while also opening opportunities for fintechs leveraging AI for optimization and new service creation.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Value in Payments Accrues to Software-Led Players with Durable Moats
viewpoints.description: McKinsey argues that value will increasingly accrue to players that combine software capabilities with harder-to-replicate moats such as proprietary data, embedded distribution, trusted customer relationships, and deep workflow integration. This implies that in a slower-growth, fee-led payments market, capturing value depends less on proximity to the end user and more on these durable advantages. Digital financial services and embedded finance providers with strong software integration and sticky customer relationships are better positioned for long-term success.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: India's UPI-led Instant Payment System Shows Aggressive A2A Adoption
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights India (UPI) as an instant-dominant market where low-cost, state-orchestrated real-time account-to-account (A2A) infrastructures have achieved massive public scale. A2A adoption is expected to climb to very high levels by 2030 and 2035, absorbing remaining cash flows. This widespread adoption of open-access rails eliminates interchange friction and provides a fertile ground for direct software and agent integration, which is highly positive for the growth and innovation of digital financial services in India.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Connected Digital Infrastructure Key to India's B2B Commerce and Credit Growth
viewpoints.description: Bain & Company asserts that a connected digital ecosystem is a critical force multiplier for India's business sector, especially for B2B commerce, payments, and credit. This infrastructure can reduce information asymmetry, strengthen supply chain resilience, and improve access to working capital, supporting more informed commercial and credit decisions. This is a highly positive outlook for digital financial services, particularly digital credit platforms targeting MSMEs, as it creates a foundation for scalable, efficient, and formal lending.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: Interoperable Layer to Enable Confident Cash-Flow Based Lending for MSMEs
viewpoints.description: Bain & Company posits that an interoperable unifying layer connecting business systems and banks can digitize the entire order-to-cash cycle for B2B transactions. This shared platform, built on common standards and APIs, will create a verifiable trail of invoice, payment, and adjustment data. This shared visibility and trust will give lenders a more current view of cash flows, enabling more confident and accurate credit decisions for thin-file MSMEs, which directly benefits digital credit platforms and financial inclusion efforts.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: Generative AI and Analytics Poised to Compound B2B Lending Gains
viewpoints.description: Bain & Company predicts that advanced analytics and generative AI will compound gains across the B2B ecosystem. These technologies can enable cash-flow intelligence, dynamic risk scoring, agentic credit underwriting, and open-market intelligence. Over time, agentic AI could orchestrate the entire trade lifecycle end-to-end. This is a strong positive for digital financial services, especially digital credit platforms, as it promises to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and accessibility of lending through sophisticated technological applications.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: Fintech Investment Rebounding, Concentrated in Scalable Platforms and AI
viewpoints.description: KPMG reports that global fintech investment is regaining momentum, with H1 2026 seeing a significant increase in capital deployed, signaling growing investor confidence. However, deal volumes remain soft, indicating a concentration of capital on large deals for mature fintechs with well-proven business models and scalable platforms, particularly in AI. This suggests a maturing sector where established digital financial services companies leveraging AI for efficiency and growth will attract substantial funding, while early-stage ventures might face more selective investor scrutiny.

viewpoints.title: Payments Viewed as Platform for Scalable Growth with Value in Embedded Services
viewpoints.description: KPMG indicates that organizations are increasingly viewing payments as a platform for scalable growth and innovation, with the biggest opportunities residing in the services built around the payment rail itself. The focus is shifting towards outcomes like cash flow optimization, faster receivables, more efficient payment workflows, and industry-specific value propositions. This perspective strongly favors digital financial services that provide embedded finance and value-added services built on payment infrastructure, moving beyond mere transaction processing to deliver comprehensive solutions.

viewpoints.title: B2B Payments Market Remains Hot, Investors Highly Selective on Pain Points
viewpoints.description: KPMG notes that the B2B payments space continues to attract significant interest from investors. However, investors are becoming highly selective, channeling capital into companies that demonstrate a proven ability to solve real pain points within the payments ecosystem, particularly those related to cross-border payments, foreign exchange, and treasury management. This indicates a maturing market for B2B digital financial services, where innovative solutions addressing complex operational challenges will find strong support, but undifferentiated offerings may struggle to attract investment.

viewpoints.title: Businesses Demand Integrated FX, Liquidity, and AI-Enabled Financial Tools
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that internationally active midsize companies require more than just low-cost cross-border payments; they need comprehensive tools to manage FX exposure, liquidity, and cash flows across multiple markets. These businesses increasingly expect intelligent, AI-enabled recommendations for real-time decision-making. This creates a significant opportunity for digital financial services platforms to offer sophisticated embedded finance solutions that combine payment execution with advisory services, workflow automation, and advanced analytics, moving beyond basic transaction utilities to integrated financial management.
viewpoints.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

viewpoints.title: Microfinance Sector Showing Growth Revival with Stronger Operating Environment
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings reports that the microfinance sector is exhibiting early signs of growth revival, with improving disbursements and AUM. The sector is entering FY27 with a structurally stronger operating environment compared to FY24, attributed to tighter lending practices, greater product diversification, and robust technology-enabled credit controls. This positive shift is driven by the clean-up of stressed portfolios and healthier new originations, indicating a more disciplined and resilient foundation for financial inclusion tech and digital lending within the microfinance space.
viewpoints.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead

viewpoints.title: NBFC-MFIs Diversifying into Individual and Non-Microfinance Lending Segments
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings observes a structural development where NBFC-MFIs are gradually diversifying into individual lending and non-microfinance segments, reducing their reliance on Joint Liability Group (JLG) based lending. This is enabled by the relaxation of qualifying-asset requirements. Larger institutions are particularly benefiting from this trend due to stronger capital, lower funding costs, and better risk management. This indicates an evolution in digital credit platforms and financial inclusion tech, expanding their product offerings beyond traditional microfinance to broader retail lending.
viewpoints.source_title: Microfinance: Out of the Woods? Assessing the Road Ahead
